clinician.final_diagnosis: Varicella (chickenpox) with bullous impetigo due to Staphylococcus aureus superinfection in a child with atopic dermatitis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 3-year-old non-VZV-vaccinated girl with mild atopic dermatitis (SCORAD <25) presented to the Pediatric Dermatology Outpatient Clinic with high-grade fever and a new generalized bullous rash. Clinical examination revealed 2–5 cm diameter flaccid bullae with hypopyon sign (pus-fluid level in dependent part), a single plump blister on intact skin as the primary lesion, and disseminated pinhead-sized papules, vesicles, pustules, erosions, and crusts with erythema. Palms, soles, scalp, genital, and oral mucosa were spared. On admission, VZV infection was confirmed by PCR from both serum and blisters (E002), and VZV serology demonstrated recent infection with positive IgM and negative IgG antibodies (E003). Bacterial culture from skin smear revealed superinfection with Staphylococcus aureus without methicillin resistance (E004), confirming bullous impetigo. The patient was isolated in the pediatric ward and treated with IV acyclovir 130 mg TID (10 mg/kg/day) and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 650 mg TID (50 mg/kg/day) for 5 days. She recovered completely after 10 days, with only residual eczema plaques from the known atopic dermatitis persisting (E009).
